task: Deepen (flagship 10) open-tennis-robots: why one 1,107 rpm wheel read 1.48x its drop through the loop fit; a tach averaging a fixed time
errors: Ran `git stash` to measure main's wheel_loop_sweep while two background simulator sweeps and the unit suite were running; they had already imported their modules so results were unaffected, but it was a risk.

First enabled TACH_WINDOW_US 40 ms and HOLD_RPM 3,000 together and ran the 9-build drill; the drop fits got much worse, so four isolation runs were needed to attribute it to the window. Changing two things before the drill check cost about 30 minutes.

doc_friction.issue: "Slow wheels need slower gains" says tests/wheel_loop_sweep.py reads 2.6% worst at the gate; main reads 3.3% today. Noted in the new section rather than rewriting history.

Its ESC-lag plant runs with the board told no ESC lag (LaunchCheck.esc_tau_us 0), which a deployed board would set from its survey; conclusions drawn from it about the hold flip once the lag is told. Worth a --told flag.

writeups: ventures/open-tennis-robots/firmware/esp32/README.md ("The 1.48x wheel", "A tach that averages a fixed time")
notes: Cause of the 1.48x wheel: unheld at 1,107 rpm (HOLD_RPM 1,000), snapshot froze 0.16 s after the ball, 3 recovery revolutions, tau pinned at 0.1 s grid floor. HOLD_RPM -> 3,000. Told-lag nine builds: spin err at floor 1,000 0.55 -> 0.39% mean, worst 1.72 -> 1.74%. Untold lag: worse (1.46 -> 2.10%). Fixed-time tach built, measured, shipped off (40 ms: gate over-3% 14 -> 7 of 336, worst 7.0 -> 3.3%, but drop fits 3-5% low behind an untold ESC lag). Verification: run_venture_tests.py open-tennis-robots 341 tests OK (58 skipped, build123d); run_workflow_locally.py --for-changes: see PR.
